searchText: I'm struggling to find a reason why this fork started. Teku considers every bock on the chain lighthouse views as canonical as valid and seems to be consistently converging on it. Now that there is a very long period of non-finalization some known limitations are causing lots of trouble (mostly that Teku requires a lot of memory and a few other smaller things). If it was a fork choice bug, then Teku should have had both sets of blocks but be selecting the wrong one but the teku instances don't appear to have any blocks from the other fork at all. ok, found one of my nodes that does have both sides of the fork and Sunday night was picking the wrong one. Today though, without connecting to any other peers, it's picking the right one. So that brings us back to a fork choice bug - just not going to be particularly easy to find it... So I'm going back through the logs to see when things first went wrong, and the odd thing is that even at slot 141298, my Teku node is agreeing on the same block as Lighthouse (this is as the slots actually happen, it may have reorg'd later). That's in epoch 4415 but we still have only finalized epoch 4410 - it should have finalized up to 4413 by now. In fact even in epoch 4420 we're still agreeing. The first suspicious thing I can see is that Teku rejects an attestation as invalid around slot 141457 by which time we've got 8 epochs that have failed to finalize. Given Teku was following the chain correctly up until that point and lighthouse and prysm seem to agree, why didn't it finalize? Even after that rejection, in real time Teku reported an empty slot at 141457 when it should have had a block. It caught up again though because it's in sync at 141495. What eventually takes Teku out is that it currently has to hold all hot blocks & states in memory so runs out of memory and GC consumes most of the CPU so things fall behind with lots of empty slots. But all of that is because the chain wasn't finalizing, and at least this teku node didn't cause the lack of finalization so I'm still very unclear what originally triggered the issue. If anyone has Teku logs between May 17 1100->1300 I'd love to get a copy please. How is Schlesi doing? Any ideas on this? hmm it should be sorted, afaik. are all the blocks your received unsorted, or is it only a portion of the batch ? <@!118185622543269890> Still no finality. Getting the Teku validators back online now will need a lot of ram (I've got one tracking head again but threw 20Gb at it - it's using 6-8 Gb of that but it definitely needs more than a 4Gb VM). That memory usage is a known limitation - we hold all non-finalised states in memory so when finalization is delayed memory usage goes up. excerpts.content: I'm struggling to find a reason why this fork started.  Teku considers every bock on the chain lighthouse views as canonical as valid and seems to be consistently converging on it.  Now that there is a very long period of non-finalization some known limitations are causing lots of trouble (mostly that Teku requires a lot of memory and a few other smaller things).

Today though, without connecting to any other peers, it's picking the right one.  So that brings us back to a fork choice bug - just not going to be particularly easy to find it...

That's in epoch 4415 but we still have only finalized epoch 4410 - it should have finalized up to 4413 by now.  In fact even in epoch 4420 we're still agreeing.  The first suspicious thing I can see is that Teku rejects an attestation as invalid around slot 141457 by which time we've got 8 epochs that have failed to finalize.
